scope: 29 individually judged stranded members; two confirmed-malicious parent archive verdicts retained.
method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md; atomscan slow scans and cleave facts for each supplied member and parent; source control-flow tracing, original-archive byte comparisons, decoded text inspection, ZIP central/local record inspection and bounded DEFLATE probes. No sample code was executed and no payload peer was contacted. Final rescans explicitly disable reference following.

changes.ssi: Move SSI exec-cmd syntax to the neutral shell-command capability, preserving its matcher, type and OS scope. Notable replaces suspicious because a fixed SSI command is an ordinary page-generation capability; it proves neither injection nor execution. Keep the hostile HTTP-variable-command composite and update its exact dependency.
changes.alert_syntax: Move three alert-source observations from offensive-tool identity into source-call syntax metadata. Preserve regexes, decoded matching, count threshold, max size, type and platform gates, criticalities, and explicit consumers. Repeated alert syntax does not prove an alert-only payload, harmlessness or a tool identity.
changes.directory_consumers: Generic offensive-tool directory selectors no longer inherit alert source syntax; this corrects their claimed identity boundary. Freeze the existing PHP-panel source-call exclusion population so new syntax observations do not broaden it.

validation_controls.existing_control_result: Normalized findings unchanged; the XXE and invisible-Unicode attack controls retain their detections. HTTP-fed SSI control retains its hostile execution finding.
validation_controls.alert_padding: A new hostile PHP request-command fixture retains hostile detection even alongside ten alert calls. Source shape does not establish tool identity or benign intent.

coverage_limits: The traversal ZIPs have one distinct hostile defacement behavior and one built-in suspicious path-traversal observation each. Adding a second hostile for the same escape/overwrite would duplicate evidence.

The three C stubs and hidden.php have several findings for a narrow single-purpose payload. They do not support invented C2, persistence, evasion or extra privilege exploits merely to reach a behavior count.
PHP flow extraction reports source-local/field and parse limitations. Direct code inspection supplies the request-to-command/callable and socket-to-pipe relationships; runtime success is not assumed.
The engine warns that the installed v18 model specification is older than the v19 feature extractor; retain this calibration limitation when reading classifier probabilities.

members.note: Laudanum PHP shell: HTTP commands gated by IP and password

members.note: WordPress shell: HTTP command payload locks its own file
members.behavior: Cheap & Nasty WordPress Shell plugin 0.3 by Leon Jacobs. At load, system calls remove write permissions and set the immutable bit on __FILE__. A configurable $_REQUEST command key reaches executeCommand, which tries ReflectionFunction(system)->invoke, call_user_func_array/system, call_user_func/system, passthru, then system. No request authentication is implemented. A second branch attempts fsockopen plus /bin/sh -i descriptor-3 redirection, but $ip is uninitialized when first used as a request key and the port lookup uses the value 443 as its key; reverse-shell success is not established. The command endpoint and anti-deletion operations independently support the verdict.

members.note: Laudanum ASPX shell: header-gated HTTP cmd /c execution
members.behavior: Laudanum ASP.NET shell. Page_Load takes the first X-Forwarded-For header value, if supplied, in preference to UserHostAddress, then compares it with loopback/private allowed IPs. Unauthorized clients get 404. POST field c constructs ProcessStartInfo("cmd", "/c " + Request.Form["c"]), disables UseShellExecute, redirects stdout/stderr, suppresses the process window, calls Start and returns both streams. UseShellExecute=false does not prevent cmd.exe from interpreting its /c text. The IP gate can trust attacker-controlled forwarding information unless deployment supplies a sanitizing proxy; that deployment is unknown.

members.note: Laudanum WP reverse shell: POST-selected socket relays shell I/O
members.behavior: Laudanum WordPress template of Pentestmonkey PHP reverse shell. POST ip and port choose the peer, with fallback 10.2.2.1:8888. The script has no local auth/IP-check include. It removes execution time limits; optionally forks and setsid; changes cwd to / and umask to zero; opens fsockopen; starts "uname -a; w; id; /bin/sh -i" using proc_open. Nonblocking stream_select relays socket reads to child stdin and child stdout/stderr back to the same socket. Forking is ordinary daemonization, not proof of persistence or analysis evasion.

display_differences: The final --follow=none pipeline omits redundant any/needs summaries and unconsumed low-tier observations. archive_comparison_notes: All hostile/suspicious observations survive after the explicit SSI capability correction. The confirmed parent verdicts are retained, not re-judged.

The initial scans followed references from the supplied environment. The initial archive scan included four GitHub Actions registry documents. Final scans use --follow=none and exclude those external records; per-file display differences are recorded with retained evidence.

Redundant CI summary findings are omitted in the final archive presentation: runner-context, contents-write, mutable-action and stage-all unions retain their respective path, job permission, version/master reference and script-command atoms. The omitted wget word component retains actual wget/download observations. These are presentation/context differences, not removed attack capabilities.
The alert-source identity correction exposes a notable Startup batch-file path in the separate XSS-EnDe-h4k reference list; that literal-path observation is accurate and is retained.

Both full-archive scans report a hard timeout in the unchanged PHP stream-base64-encode-filter rule on large wordlist data. Direct scans of every requested member completed; no requested payload detection loss was observed. This archive-wide analysis limit is not repaired by inventing YAML behavior.
